Fast duplicate-account-address detection with AVX and hash-table fallback.

# Purpose
`fd_chkdup.h` defines the duplicate-account check used during transaction packing. It provides the public interface for creating, joining, leaving, and deleting a `fd_chkdup_t` object, and for checking one or two lists of account addresses for repeated entries. The code is written as a header-only interface so the functions can be inlined, since the check is on the critical path for transaction sanitization. It also defines the required scratch memory footprint and alignment, and it uses a fixed-size internal state that includes a hash map and, on SIMD-capable platforms, per-instance entropy for the fast path.

The file contains both a fast duplicate test and a precise fallback test. On AVX or AVX512 systems, [`fd_chkdup_check_fast`](<#fd_chkdup_check_fast>) uses SIMD bit tests as a Bloom-filter-like precheck that can return false positives but not false negatives. [`fd_chkdup_check`](<#fd_chkdup_check>) calls the fast path first and then calls [`fd_chkdup_check_slow`](<#fd_chkdup_check_slow>) only when needed. The slow path uses an internal hash map to detect exact duplicates and also handles invalid account addresses. The file therefore exposes a narrow API for duplicate detection, while also containing the full implementation logic and platform-specific SIMD code needed to make the check fast.
